entry.title: Combined summary - Silent Payments Sender - BIP352 plugin for Electrum
entry.summary: The Electrum Silent Payments Sender plugin introduces BIP352 Silent Payments directly into the Electrum desktop wallet, enabling users to send funds to Silent Payment addresses without leaving the familiar Send tab interface. This integration streamlines the user experience and brings advanced privacy-focused payment capabilities to Electrum users. The plugin operates on Electrum versions 4.6.0 and above and is compatible with Bitcoin’s mainnet, testnet, signet, and regtest networks. Functionality is currently confined to standard single-signature deterministic software wallets, accommodating multiple input types such as P2PKH, P2WPKH-P2SH, and P2WPKH. Users can initiate transactions using either raw addresses or by employing BIP21 `sp` payment instructions, broadening its practical utility for diverse payment scenarios. However, several wallet types and features remain unsupported. Hardware wallets, watch-only setups, imported-key wallets, multisig configurations, and 2FA-protected accounts cannot utilize this plugin at present. Key functionalities like Taproot input processing, batching of payments, payjoin, swaps, as well as unsigned preview/export or deferred transaction signing are not available in the current release. Security remains a critical consideration. As the plugin has not undergone a formal security audit, caution is advised. Installation requires downloading the latest version from the [Releases](https://github.com/ZenulAbidin/electrum-silent-payments-sender/releases/) page on GitHub, followed by verification of the SHA256 file hash. This verification step is essential for ensuring the integrity of the downloaded file, though it is only effective if the expected hash originates from a trusted, independent source. Relying solely on hashes provided alongside the download may not be sufficient protection against compromised releases. Stronger verification methods, such as signed releases or reproducible builds, are particularly important for plugins that interact with sensitive wallet keys. Once downloaded and verified, the plugin can be installed through Electrum's Tools menu under Plugins, where users select and enable the appropriate zip file. This approach ensures seamless integration into existing workflows, allowing users to benefit from enhanced privacy features with minimal disruption. Maintaining best practices for software verification and remaining attentive to future updates and audits will further strengthen security when adopting new wallet plugins.
